meta.dataset: Florida Senate Local Funding Initiative Requests (LFIR) — Clay County, FY2026-27
meta.methodology: Clay County LFIR rows were identified by scraping the server-rendered HTML table at the official Florida Senate LocalFundingRequests listing page for FY2026-27 and FY2025-26 (search terms: 'Clay', 'Green Cove Springs', 'Orange Park', 'Keystone Heights', 'Fleming Island', 'Middleburg', 'Penney Farms', 'Black Creek'). Every FY2026-27 Clay-relevant LFIR was then downloaded as an individual PDF directly from flsenate.gov (canonical URL pattern: https://www.flsenate.gov/PublishedContent/Session/FiscalYear/FY2026-27/LocalFundingInitiativeRequests/FY2026-27_S<LFIR#>.pdf) and parsed with pdftotext. Legislative outcome (vetoed) was cross-checked against the official Governor's veto list (flgov.com, 2026 Veto List.pdf), which cites both House Form (HF) and Senate Form (SF) numbers per line item, letting each veto entry be matched back to its LFIR by the SF number.
meta.totalRequestedAmountNote: Sum of the 19 unique active FY2026-27 Clay-related LFIR 'Total State Funds Requested' figures (question #6 on each form). Excludes LFIR #2960 ($750,000), which the Senate's own listing marks '(withdrawn) duplicates' of #3085 (same Moccasin Slough project, refiled one day later) — counting both would double-count.
meta.sessionContext: FY2026-27 LFIRs were filed 11/21/2025-12/3/2025, ahead of the 2026 regular session. The FY2026-27 General Appropriations Act (originally filed as HB 5001; the flsenate.gov bill-history page for HB 5001 shows it 'Died in Conference Committee' 3/13/2026 with a note pointing to a companion/renumbered bill) was ultimately signed by Governor DeSantis on 2026-06-29 as a $117.6B budget, with a reported $800M-$1.7B in line-item vetoes (news sources give different totals: Florida Phoenix reported ~$1.7B, Florida Politics/AP-wire coverage reported ~$1.6B, and the Governor's own office language cited in coverage says 'nearly $810 million' in local-project line-item vetoes specifically, which is a subset of the larger total that also includes fund transfers like $750M to the Budget Stabilization Fund). This fork could not obtain and grep the full enacted GAA line-by-line within its scope — see 'stillNeeded' below. Only the veto list itself was obtained and searched directly.

notFoundOrRuledOut: No Clay-relevant FY2026-27 LFIR titled or referencing 'Black Creek' was found in the Senate table search — the Black Creek Water Resource Development Project (SJRWMD) appears to be funded/tracked through a different mechanism (District budget + a legacy multi-year legislative appropriation from ~2017), not this cycle's LFIR process. Left to the fork covering Part I.

No 'CCUA Interconnect' or Clay-titled item under sponsors other than Jennifer Bradley was found — all 19 active Clay-relevant FY2026-27 LFIRs share the same sponsor, consistent with Bradley representing SD6 (Clay + Baker, Bradford, Union, Columbia, Gilchrist, part of Alachua/Duval).

'Penney Farms', 'Middleburg' (as a standalone project title), and 'Fleming Island' (as a standalone project title) did not independently match any FY2026-27 LFIR beyond what's already captured (CR 218 references the Clay Hill/Middleburg community in its description; Moccasin Slough is located on Fleming Island).
stillNeeded: The enacted FY2026-27 General Appropriations Act (its final chapter-law text — bill numbering was confusing to trace: flsenate.gov shows the originally filed HB 5001 as having 'died in conference committee' 3/13/2026, implying the actual enacted bill was a renumbered/special-session vehicle; this needs a records request or a more careful LegiScan/Laws-of-Florida lookup) needs to be searched line-by-line for 'Clay County' to determine, for the 15 LFIRs marked 'appropriationStatus: unknown' above, whether each was (a) appropriated and survived, or (b) never made it into the conference budget at all. Right now only the 4 vetoed line items are confirmed.

FY2025-26, FY2024-25, FY2023-24, FY2022-23, and earlier LFIR cycles were not swept with the same full-PDF-download rigor as FY2026-27 — only a table-level pass was done for FY2025-26. A thorough multi-year sweep (per the original mission's 'search the entire system' instruction) would need each fiscal year's table scraped the same way FY2026-27 was.

Confirmation of 'actual funds received' (vs. appropriated) for any surviving line item would require Clay County's own budget/CIP documents or the state agency's grant-disbursement records — LFIR/GAA/veto records only show REQUESTED → (possibly) APPROPRIATED → (possibly) VETOED, never RECEIVED or SPENT.

The Fleet Center (#2951) federal match ($1,500,000, 50%) description doesn't specify the federal program/grant it would come from — worth a follow-up records request to Clay County OEM or Fire Rescue.

News coverage (First Coast News, 'What Jacksonville area projects got nixed?') was blocked (HTTP 403) and could not be read directly — it may contain additional named Clay-area vetoes/survivals beyond what the primary veto-list PDF search surfaced by title-string match alone (e.g., if a title was phrased differently there than in the LFIR).
